messages:
sara: Thanks everyone for joining the security/privacy/compliance Q&A after the all-hands. I'll drop notes here and @alex/meera/juan will answer live. Please keep questions short and we’ll follow up on threads.

sam: Quick one to start — SOC2 and ISO roadmap?

alex: SOC2 Type I completed Jan 2024. Targeting SOC2 Type II audit completion by Q4 2024.

meera: For ISO27001 we're in gap analysis now, aiming for certification in H1 2025.

sam: Nice — will Type II cover Hosted + Dedicated?

alex: Yes, scope includes Hosted API and Dedicated. Private (customer-managed) has a narrower scope; we provide artifacts and controls but customers with on-prem may need complementary evidence.

juan: On VPC/private deployment questions — we support Private control plane over customer VPC and an on-prem package. Networking diagram and setup guide will be in the private-deploy repo by end of month.

sara: @juan can you clarify the VPC peering vs. PrivateLink recommendation for AWS customers?

juan: Recommend PrivateLink for cross-account isolation; peering ok for simple setups but harder to scale. We'll publish a decision matrix.

sam: Audit logs — retention, export options?

meera: Default audit log retention is 90 days for Hosted. Enterprise customers can choose configurable retention up to 7 years via the Console. Exports: S3 lifecycle export (parquet) and streaming to customer SIEM via our webhook/Kinesis connector.

alex: There's also an audit-logs API: GET /v1/audit-logs with filters (user, resource, action, time range). We'll add RBAC so only authorized roles can pull full logs.

sam: KMS / CMK — can customers bring their own key? how does rotation work?

juan: Yes, KMS integrations are supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we currently support Customer-Managed Keys via AWS KMS for encryption-at-rest for customer-specific data (not global model weights). Rotation: automatic yearly rotation if enabled in KMS, and we log key-change events in audit logs.

sam: Any sample config?

juan: Example for private deploy (YAML):
```
encryption:
  kms_provider: aws
  kms_key_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
  key_policy: customer_managed
```

meera: Note: we never send raw plaintext keys to Redwood. We hand off to customer KMS or generate envelope keys and store only encrypted material.

alex: Pen tests and external audits — we run quarterly internal scans and annual 3rd-party pentests. Customers can request an audited SOC2 package + pen test summary under NDA.

sara: Are there any immediate changes to customer defaults we should know about?

meera: No breaking defaults. We're rolling out opt-in features: KMS CMK for hosted (pilot in June), longer audit retention as an enterprise toggle, and PrivateLink templates in the Console.

sam: Will the Console show per-token access logs for debugging?

alex: Yes — Console will have token-level access log view (request metadata only: client IP range, model, route, tokens). We won't surface prompt contents by default; you can enable higher-fidelity logs with customer consent for debugging.

sam: Legal/compliance question — can we sign data processing addendums for EU customers?

meera: Yes, DPAs and standard contractual clauses available. For High-Compliance customers we offer isolated regions + dedicated capacity.

sara: Thanks all. Action items: @alex to publish SOC2 Type II timeline doc, @juan to share VPC/PrivateLink decision matrix and YAML examples, @meera to upload DPA checklist. We'll follow up with a Confluence page and a short FAQ.

deploy-bot: Reminder: Security roadmap doc uploaded to //confluence.redwood/sec-roadmap (new file). :memo:

sam: :thumbsup:

alex: I'll post the audit-logs API spec tomorrow and tag this thread.

meera: Will also attach the DPA template.

sara: Closing the live thread — thanks for the great questions! If anyone needs 1:1s, ping me.
